`taxastand` matches names against a reference taxonomy that you supply. This vignette shows the ways to set one up, from a named source to your own table.


``` r
library(taxastand)
library(dplyr)

# Downloads go here. By default they go to a temporary folder.
cache_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "taxastand-vignette")
```

## What a reference needs

A reference is a data frame in [Darwin Core](https://dwc.tdwg.org/) format with these columns:

- `taxonID`: a unique ID for each name
- `acceptedNameUsageID`: for a synonym, the `taxonID` of its accepted name; for an accepted name, its own ID (or `NA`)
- `taxonomicStatus`: `"accepted"` or a synonym status
- `scientificName`: the name **with its author**, such as `"Polypodium vulgare L."`

The author must be part of `scientificName`, because `taxastand` matches on it. Many databases keep the author in a separate column, `scientificNameAuthorship`; `ts_format_ref()` combines them.

## Named sources

`ts_show_ref_sources()` lists the sources that `ts_load_ref()` can download, with their licenses:


``` r
ts_show_ref_sources() |>
  select(source, name, license)
#>   source                                                 name      license
#> 1    wfo                        World Flora Online Plant List      CC0 1.0
#> 2    ppg Pteridophyte Phylogeny Group classification (PPG II)    CC BY 4.0
#> 3   itis       Integrated Taxonomic Information System (ITIS)      CC0 1.0
#> 4    col                              Catalogue of Life (COL)    CC BY 4.0
#> 5   gbif                               GBIF Backbone Taxonomy    CC BY 4.0
#> 6   ncbi                                        NCBI Taxonomy      CC0 1.0
#> 7    ott                             Open Tree Taxonomy (OTT)      CC0 1.0
#> 8     fb                                             FishBase CC BY-NC 4.0
#> 9    slb                                          SeaLifeBase CC BY-NC 4.0
```

PPG (the Pteridophyte Phylogeny Group classification of ferns and lycophytes) is small, so it makes a good first try:


``` r
ppg <- ts_load_ref(source = "ppg", cache_dir = cache_dir)
#> Downloading https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pteridogroup/ppg/v2.1.0/data/ppg.csv
#> Loaded 74784 names from Pteridophyte Phylogeny Group classification (PPG II) (version v2.1.0), license CC BY 4.0.
#> Please cite: Pteridophyte Phylogeny Group. PPG taxonomic database. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22760360
count(ppg, taxonomicStatus)
#>   taxonomicStatus     n
#> 1        accepted 15219
#> 2         synonym 55064
#> 3       unchecked  4501
```

The file is downloaded once and kept in `cache_dir`; later calls reuse it. The source of the data is stored with the result, for citing:


``` r
attr(ppg, "ts_source")[c("name", "version", "license", "url")]
#> $name
#> [1] "Pteridophyte Phylogeny Group classification (PPG II)"
#> 
#> $version
#> [1] "v2.1.0"
#> 
#> $license
#> [1] "CC BY 4.0"
#> 
#> $url
#> [1] "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pteridogroup/ppg/v2.1.0/data/ppg.csv"
```

To get an older version, use `ts_show_ref_sources(versions = TRUE)` to see what is available, and provide your selection to the `version` argument of `ts_load_ref()`.

### Keep only part of a large source

Large sources have millions of names. Specify `taxon` (and optionally `rank`) to keep only a family or other group, with its synonyms:


``` r
itis <- ts_load_ref(source = "itis", taxon = "Polypodiaceae", cache_dir = cache_dir)
#> Downloading https://data.source.coop/cboettig/taxadb/2026/dwc_itis_part_0.parquet
#> Loaded 309 names from Integrated Taxonomic Information System (ITIS) (version 2026), license CC0 1.0.
#> Please cite: Integrated Taxonomic Information System (ITIS), https://www.itis.gov/ Accessed through taxadb: Norman, K.E.A., Chamberlain, S. & Boettiger, C. (2020) taxadb: A high-performance local taxonomic database interface. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 11: 1153-1159. https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.13440
```

Then use the reference as usual (see `vignette("basics")`):


``` r
queries <- c(
  "Polypodium vulgare L.",
  "Phymatodes scolopendria (Burm. f.) Ching",
  "Microsorum scolopendria",
  "Polypodium pelucidum Kaulf."
)
res <- ts_resolve_names(queries, itis, match_no_auth = TRUE)
res[match(queries, res$query), c("query", "resolved_name", "matched_status", "match_type")]
#>                                      query
#> 1                    Polypodium vulgare L.
#> 4 Phymatodes scolopendria (Burm. f.) Ching
#> 2                  Microsorum scolopendria
#> 3              Polypodium pelucidum Kaulf.
#>                               resolved_name matched_status  match_type
#> 1                     Polypodium vulgare L.       accepted       exact
#> 4 Microsorum scolopendria (Burm. f.) Copel.        synonym       exact
#> 2 Microsorum scolopendria (Burm. f.) Copel.       accepted auto_noauth
#> 3              Polypodium pellucidum Kaulf.       accepted  auto_fuzzy
```

Some sources are Parquet files. These need the [nanoparquet](https://nanoparquet.r-lib.org/) or [duckdb](https://r.duckdb.org/) package; with duckdb, `taxon` is applied while reading, which is faster for very large files. `ts_load_ref()` says which package to install if neither is available.

Downloaded files can be listed with `ts_show_ref_cache()` and deleted with `ts_clear_ref_cache()`.

## Your own file or URL

`ts_load_ref()` also reads a CSV or TSV file (`file =`) or downloads one from an HTTPS address (`url =`). If the columns have other names, map them to Darwin Core names with `col_map`; each name is the Darwin Core name and each value is your column:


``` r
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
write.csv(
  data.frame(
    id = c("1", "2", "3"), accepted_id = c("1", "1", "3"),
    status = c("Accepted", "Synonym", "Accepted"),
    name = c("Polypodium vulgare", "Polypodium rotundatum", "Pteris vittata"),
    author = c("L.", "Willd.", "L."),
    family = c("Polypodiaceae", NA, "Pteridaceae")
  ),
  f,
  row.names = FALSE
)

own <- ts_load_ref(
  file = f,
  col_map = c(
    taxonID = "id", acceptedNameUsageID = "accepted_id",
    taxonomicStatus = "status", scientificName = "name",
    scientificNameAuthorship = "author"
  ),
  version = "my-table"
)
own
#>   taxonID acceptedNameUsageID taxonomicStatus               scientificName
#> 1       1                   1        accepted        Polypodium vulgare L.
#> 2       2                   1         synonym Polypodium rotundatum Willd.
#> 3       3                   3        accepted            Pteris vittata L.
#>          family
#> 1 Polypodiaceae
#> 2          <NA>
#> 3   Pteridaceae
```

## Steps by hand

`ts_load_ref()` combines two steps that you can also use on any data frame, for example one you made yourself or got from another package:

- `ts_subset_ref(ref, taxon)` keeps the members of a taxon and their synonyms. It uses columns for higher ranks (such as `family`) if there are any, otherwise walks down from the taxon using `parentNameUsageID`.
- `ts_format_ref(ref)` formats the data so that `taxastand` can use it for name matching and resolution: it applies `col_map`, adds the author to the name, drops rows above species rank, keeps the needed columns and tidies values.

If your table has only `parentNameUsageID` and no columns for higher ranks, subset first, because formatting drops the rows above species that are needed to find the members of a taxon.


``` r
own |>
  ts_subset_ref("Pteridaceae") |>
  select(taxonID, scientificName, family)
#>   taxonID    scientificName      family
#> 3       3 Pteris vittata L. Pteridaceae
```

## Other packages and databases

Any other source works the same way: get a data frame, then pass it to `ts_format_ref()`. As an example, the [taxadb](https://docs.ropensci.org/taxadb/) package provides versioned snapshots of several databases ([Catalog of Life](https://www.catalogueoflife.org/), [GBIF](https://www.gbif.org/), [NCBI](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/taxonomy), [Open Tree of Life](https://tree.opentreeoflife.org/) and others). Ask taxadb for the Darwin Core (`dwc`) schema:


``` r
library(taxadb)

taxadb_itis <- taxa_tbl(provider = "itis", schema = "dwc") |>
  filter(family == "Polypodiaceae") |>
  collect() |>
  ts_format_ref(source = list(provider = "ITIS", version = "2026 (via taxadb)"))

nrow(taxadb_itis)
#> [1] 309
```

This gives the same names as `ts_load_ref(source = "itis")`. Use taxadb for providers that `ts_load_ref()` does not list; check `colnames()` of the table first, since columns differ between databases.

## Check and edit

`ts_format_ref()` does not check that the table is valid; for example, a synonym could point to an accepted name that is missing. The [dwctaxon](https://docs.ropensci.org/dwctaxon/) package can validate Darwin Core taxonomic data (`dwctaxon::dct_validate()`) and edit it, for example to add a name that your source lacks.

## Large references

Before matching, `taxastand` parses the reference names and builds the keys it compares them with. With a reference the size of PPG or WFO this takes longer than the matching itself. If you will match several batches of queries against the same reference, optimize it once with `ts_optimize_ref()` and pass the result in place of the reference:


``` r
itis_prepared <- ts_optimize_ref(itis)
res <- ts_resolve_names(queries, itis_prepared, match_no_auth = TRUE)
```

The results are the same as without optimizing. The genus of every name is found up front, and each genus is parsed the first time a query needs it, so the first batch pays for the genera it uses and later batches reuse them. The optimized reference therefore grows as it is used. If you optimize a reference with `strip_qualifiers = TRUE`, the qualifiers are removed from the reference names when they are parsed.

## Reproducibility

Record the source and version with your results, so that the reference is the same the next time you run the analysis. `ts_load_ref()` stores them in the `ts_source` attribute (see above). Give `version =` to get the same snapshot again, and cite the database and, if you used it, taxadb. Check each source's license before reusing a table.

The results in this vignette were made with taxastand 2.0.0.9000, ITIS snapshot 2026, and taxadb 0.3.0.
